title: FinCEN cybersecurity incident, Nov 2026
disclaimer: Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by FinCEN, the US Treasury, any news outlet, regulator, company, or anyone else named.
size_basis: Potential only. FinCEN holds national financial-crime reports, so a breach of its main databases would be a national matter, but FinCEN says there is no evidence of that so far. Known impact: some FinCEN systems offline and filing deadlines extended.
who_is_affected: Banks and other financial institutions that file Bank Secrecy Act reports with FinCEN, and anyone using its BSA E-Filing website. FinCEN says the website still works, some services may not, and deadlines are being extended for filers affected.

known.text: FinCEN says a cybersecurity incident gave someone unauthorized access to a limited part of its systems.
FinCEN has taken some systems offline; its BSA E-Filing website still works, but some services may not.
FinCEN is extending filing deadlines for filers affected by the disruption.

not_known.text: Who got in, how, and when it started.
Whether any financial reports or company-ownership records were taken. FinCEN says it has no evidence of that so far.
When all systems will be back.
Whether it is connected to the breach reported at the CIA the same week.
